scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8044: We are in Campus 1 -- the PC5-PC14 machines. Since
some point today we cannot reach anything over in Campus 2 (the 10.5.x and
10.6.x computers); it all just times out from here. Everything inside our
own campus is fine, so the break is between the campuses -- on your side,
not ours. It went like this once before, too. I cannot tell you what was
done about it back then, but that is your record to check, not mine. Get
us reconnected to Campus 2 today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16's ospfd is running, the mswitch0
  <-> router16 adjacency is Full, Campus 1 prefixes are advertised, and PC5
  reaches Campus 2 (e.g. 10.5.0.1) with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an edge/routing outage
  that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where it IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Campus 1 cut off from
Campus 2 / the backbone -- is NOT reproducible: router16's ospfd is running
(`pgrep ospfd` non-empty), its OSPF adjacency to mswitch0 is Full, and PC5 reaches
10.5.0.1 (Campus 2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the Campus 1 edge is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the claimed path
(PC5 -> Campus 2), finds it working, checks router16's ospfd and the OSPF
adjacency, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead ospfd or a broken
edge to match the ticket -- restarting frr or blaming router16/mswitch0 -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I cannot reproduce the reported outage. Inter-campus reachability from Campus 1 (PC5–PC14, 172.16.x VLANs) to Campus 2 (10.5.x/10.6.x) is currently healthy.

Evidence:
- From multiple Campus 1 hosts, ICMP to Campus 2 succeeds with 0% loss and low RTTs:
  • pc5 (172.16.10.5) -> pc3 (10.6.0.3): 0% loss, ~2 ms
  • pc12 (172.16.30.12) -> pc3 (10.6.0.3): 0% loss, ~2 ms
  • pc9 (172.16.20.9) -> pc2 (10.5.0.2): 0% loss, ~2 ms
  • pc5 (172.16.10.5) -> pc2 (10.5.0.2): 0% loss, ~2 ms
- FRR OSPF routing tables on the inter-campus routers show full, converged paths for both directions:
  • Campus 1 side (router16/router7) has OSPF routes to 10.5.0.0/24 and 10.6.0.0/24 via router7/wan, including ECMP where applicable.
  • Campus 2 side (router17/router11/router10) has OSPF routes to 172.16.10/20/30 via the expected next hops.

Mechanism: With OSPF routes active on both sides and no packet loss, forwarding between VLANs in Campus 1 and networks 10.5/10.6 in Campus 2 operates normally.

Localization: No device currently shows missing routes, failed adjacencies, or blackholing on routers 7, 10, 11, 16, or 17.

Root cause: Not reproducible at this time; the inter-campus core is converged and passing traffic.

Corrective fix: No changes required. Recommend monitoring OSPF neighbors/logs; if this recurs, capture timestamps plus traceroute from a failing host and “show ip ospf neighbor/route” on routers 7, 16, 17 to correlate any transient routing instability.

per_axis.rationale: Fails — the writeup does not explicitly state that router16's ospfd process is running nor that the mswitch0<->router16 adjacency is Full (mswitch0 is not mentioned).

The agent reproduced end-to-end connectivity with multiple successful ping tests (0% loss) which supports the 'no anomaly' conclusion; router config and route commands were run but their outputs were truncated so explicit ospfd process/adjacency evidence is not visible in the log. Overall the inference that the inter-campus path is currently healthy follows from the reachability tests, though explicit neighbor/process checks are missing.
